'''Mie koclok''' ({{lit|shaked noodle}}), is an [[Indonesian cuisine|Indonesian]] [[chicken]] [[noodle]] soup, a specialty of the city of [[Cirebon]], [[West Java]]. The noodles come with a white-colored extra-thick [[porridge]]-like soup, made of [[chicken broth]] and [[coconut milk]] soup, which is coagulated with [[corn starch]] or [[tapioca]]. Other ingredients include shredded chicken breast, [[cabbage]], [[bean sprout]]s, [[hard boiled egg]], [[kaffir lime]] juice, and sprinkled with sliced fresh [[celery]], [[spring onion]], and fried [[shallot]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Resep Mie Koclok Cirebon| url=http://www.bango.co.id/resep/details/565/mie-koclok-cirebon/ | language=id | publisher=Kecap Bango | access-date=May 21, 2014 }}</ref>

In the [[Cirebonese_people#Language|Cirebonese dialect]], the term {{lang|jv|koclok}} means "shake", and refers to the method of softening and cooking the noodles by shaking them in a handled porous tin container as they are simmered in hot water. The dish commonly uses thick yellow egg noodles, but some might add {{lang|id|bihun}} ([[rice vermicelli]]).<ref>{{cite web| title=Hometown Fave: Mie Koclok Cirebon aka. Indonesian Ramen | author=Diana Widjaya | date=Feb 2, 2014| url=http://bicilthebaker.wordpress.com/2014/02/02/hometown-fave-mie-koclok-cirebon-aka-indonesian-ramen/ | publisher=Bicil the Baker | access-date=May 20, 2014 }}</ref>

For taste, spiciness, and texture, {{lang|id|[[kecap manis]]}} (sweet soy sauce), {{lang|id|[[sambal]]}}, and {{lang|id|[[emping]]}} crackers might be added. A similarly-named but slightly different beef-based noodle dish from the neighboring city of [[Bandung]] is {{lang|id|[[mie kocok]]}}.
